what_it_does: This paper describes a phase shifter—a radio component that rotates the phase (timing) of a signal—designed for 6G wireless systems at D-band frequencies (110–170 gigahertz, which is a high-frequency band currently being explored for next-generation cellular). The key challenge is that phase shifters at these frequencies must be small, work in both transmission and reception modes, stay accurate across a wide frequency range, and not require manual calibration after manufacture. This design achieves all four goals: it can shift phases across a full 360-degree range with less than 2.38 degrees of error and less than 0.63 decibels of amplitude variation, all without needing any runtime tuning.
